title: Eight International Diwali Getaways That Can Still Fit a Rs 50,000 Budget
excerpt: Nepal and Sri Lanka are the easiest fits; Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Cambodia, Bali and even the Maldives can work per person if flights are booked early and spending stays tight.
body:
• Eight destinations can fit a Rs 50,000-per-person Diwali trip from India: Nepal, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Bali, Cambodia and the Maldives, according to Curly Tales.
  • Nepal and Sri Lanka are the most budget-friendly — short flights, low daily costs, and for Nepal no visa at all for Indians.
  • Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 this year, so the getaway window is the long weekend around it — fares decide whether the Rs 50,000 cap survives.
  • Bali and the Maldives fit only with tighter spending decisions; November is also the start of Bali's wetter season.

An international trip during the Diwali break does not have to cost a lakh. A Curly Tales roundup lists eight destinations that can fit within Rs 50,000 per person — Nepal, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Bali, Cambodia and the Maldives — provided flight prices, accommodation and travel dates cooperate.

The timing helps and hurts at once. Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8 this year, creating a natural long weekend, but festival-week fares from Indian metros are the single biggest threat to the budget. Independent budget guides make the same point: on most of these routes the return fare, booked six to ten weeks out in shoulder season, is what leaves room for hotels and food.

The easiest fits: Nepal and Sri Lanka

Nepal is the simplest trip on the list — Indians need no visa, flights from Delhi are short, and daily costs are the lowest of the eight. Sri Lanka runs a close second: round trips from Chennai, Bengaluru or Delhi are commonly quoted in the Rs 12,000–18,000 range in budget guides, with a free electronic travel authorisation and low on-the-ground costs across Colombo, Kandy and the south coast.

The Southeast Asia core

Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia and Cambodia are the value workhorses. Five-day Thailand trips are repeatedly costed at Rs 40,000–50,000 in budget guides when travellers base themselves in Bangkok or Krabi and eat street food; Malaysia fits in a Rs 35,000–50,000 band using Kuala Lumpur's cheap transit and Penang's food scene. Vietnam's challenge is the fare — once in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City, accommodation, food and local transport are inexpensive. Cambodia, anchored by Angkor Wat, often comes in comfortably under the cap for a week, with visa-on-arrival or e-visa access for Indians.

The tight squeezes: Bali and the Maldives

Bali can fit under Rs 50,000 per person with affordable flights, modest accommodation and careful spending, Curly Tales notes — with the caveat that November falls within Bali's wetter season, so travellers should plan flexible outdoor activities. The Maldives is the list's stretch option: it works only with guesthouse-island stays rather than resort islands and tight control of transfers and meals.

How to keep the trip under the cap

Three rules recur across every budget guide. Book the flight first and let it set the destination — the cheapest route on your dates wins. Stay in one base instead of adding domestic hops, which quietly add thousands. And keep a separate buffer: the Rs 50,000 figures are per-person planning estimates on twin-sharing, not package prices, and festival-week surge pricing can move them fast.
